subject: Sizing request — Dedicated GPU fleet plan for Cobalt Systems (model memory / KV cache / quantization)
messages:

Cc: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@cobaltsys.com>

Subject: Dedicated deployment sizing request — model memory & KV cache details

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Cobalt Systems is interested in a Dedicated deployment to run an internal clinical summarization pipeline. We need rough GPU fleet sizing and a pros/cons assessment tied to model memory, KV cache for long-context sessions, and quantization options so we can coordinate procurement timelines.

Key constraints:
- Model: casa-70b-32k (a Llama-family 70B variant) for generation + embedding on different routes.
- Typical prompt mix: 85% generation (avg prompt 1.2k tokens, response avg 800 tokens), 15% short-embedding calls (~256 tokens).
- Context length: 32k tokens per session (users often paste long clinical notes and want end-to-end summaries).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile generation latency < 1.2s for 8-token streaming tail (we can relax for particularly long outputs).
- Peak expected concurrency: 120 concurrent generation sessions at launch (scale target 300 in 6 months).
- Preferred deploy window: procurement/PO by end of Sept.

Questions:
1) Preliminary GPU type recommendation (A100 80GB vs H100 80GB vs alternative) and minimal vs recommended fleet size for 120 concurrency.
2) Memory math: estimate model footprint (FP16) + KV cache for 32k context and how much that changes with 4-bit GPTQ / int8 / nf4.
3) Impact on batching and throughput if we enable automatic prefix/KV caching vs not.
4) Any immediate red flags (NVMe fallback needs, PCIe bottlenecks, or licensing constraints).

I've attached a small token-profile CSV with a representative request sample and typical prompt/response length distribution. Happy to hop on a 30m call — Erin and I are free early next week.

Best,
Alex Morales\Director of Machine Learning Engineering\Cobalt Systems

Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing request — Dedicated fleet estimate and technical notes

Alex / team — uploaded the completed workbook and a short runbook summary. Key points below (high level, will follow with numbers in workbook):

1) Model & baseline memory (approx):
- casa-70b-32k (FP16 load): ~140 GB model params (unsharded), plus optimizer/overheads on host.
- With Redwood serving patterns we split model across GPUs (tensor+pipeline/sharded): effective per-GPU resident memory depends on TP/PP, but raw FP16 memory implies you need multi-GPU unless you quantize.

2) Quantization impact (practical):
- 4-bit GPTQ / NF4: model weights shrink ~3.5x — practical resident memory for weights drops to ~35–45 GB equivalent. This typically enables single-GPU residency on 80GB-class devices for inference shards (subject to KV cache).
- int8 (dynamic): ~2x reduction from FP16; good latency, smaller perf variance vs 4-bit but higher memory than 4-bit.
- Tradeoffs: 4-bit can introduce small score shifts — we advise a brief QA sweep on your prompt set (we can run comparisons in our hosted eval harness).

3) KV cache math & context sizing (32k):
- KV cache scales linearly with context length and model hidden size. For a 70B-like model with hidden size ~12k (approx), KV pairs for 32k tokens will occupy on the order of 40–60 GB of GPU memory for forward cache in FP16 per active session if cached fully on-GPU.
- Practical approach: we recommend prefix/KV caching for repeated context chunks (common in clinical workflows) and a hybrid strategy: keep recent sliding window (e.g., last 4–8k tokens) on-GPU, spill older context to extremely fast NVMe-backed local cache with prioritized prefetch for active sessions. This reduces worst-case per-session GPU RAM from 40–60 GB down to ~8–16 GB depending on cache hit rates.

4) Fleet recommendations for 120 concurrent sessions (generation-heavy) — three scenarios: minimal / recommended / throughput-optimized (numbers are initial, workbook has detailed math):
- Minimal (conservative safety): 8x A100 80GB or 6x H100 80GB, with aggressive sharding and NVMe spill enabled. Assumes use of int8 or mixed precision for generation and a 50/50 on-GPU KV cache policy.
- Recommended (balanced latency/cost): 10x H100 80GB nodes. Use 4-bit GPTQ weights for lower model residency, keep a hot KV window in GPU (~8–12k tokens), and NVMe backing for full sessions. Autoscale pool for burst to 300 concurrency.
- Throughput-optimized (latency-focused): 12+ H100 80GB with larger in-GPU KV caches and pre-warmed session pools; consider RDMA-attached NVMe for lower stall on prefetch.

5) Batching & latency:
- With a 4-bit model, operator kernels are faster and batching efficiency improves; this can reduce per-token latency for batched requests. However, 32k context means per-request compute dominates over batching for long outputs. We recommend adaptive batching (short queries batch aggressively; long sessions mostly get isolated resources).

6) Implementation caveats:
- NVMe spill requires node-level orchestration and careful prefetching — acceptable for most customers, but check compliance for disk persistence of PII. We can ensure encrypted ephemeral NVMe and automatic wipe on session termination.
- If you must avoid any disk spill, fleet size increases materially (~2–3x) because full KV caches must stay on-GPU.

Action items:
- Alex: confirm if on-disk ephemeral NVMe is allowed for your compliance team.
- Alex: if you can provide a 24-hour sample traffic trace (we used the CSV to model peaks), we’ll refine numbers to a per-hour autoscaling plan.
- Redwood: we will attach an annotated workbook with exact per-GPU memory math and a draft SOW.

Uploading: gpu-sizing-workbook.xlsx (populated) and short annotated notes.

—Monica Patel\Solutions Engineering\Redwood Inference

Alex / Erin — great to sync earlier today. Attached is the draft SOW and the finalized sizing workbook. Summary / recommended next steps: 

- Recommended starting configuration: 10x H100 80GB nodes, GPTQ 4-bit for model weights, hybrid KV strategy (8–12k hot-GPU window + encrypted NVMe backing for cold context). This meets your 95th p95 < 1.2s target for short tails and keeps headroom for autoscaling bursts to 300 concurrent sessions.
- Cost note: going 4-bit + hybrid cache reduces steady-state GPU footprint by ~40–60% vs FP16 without spill, which materially improves unit economics.
- Compliance/ops: we will provide a compliance appendix on NVMe encryption & wipe policy. If your security team disallows all disk spill we will re-run the workbook for a 100% in-GPU KV policy (expect ~2x fleet increase).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the baseline architecture (10x H100 + hybrid cache).
2) Confirm if NVMe ephemeral storage is acceptable to security/compliance.
3) If yes, we’ll circulate a PO-ready SOW (attached) for signature and propose an on-prem procurement timeline that targets hardware delivery in late-Oct and staged cutover in Nov.

Attachments: Cobalt_Dedicated_SOW_v1.pdf
